name: input.mouse.press
description: Press a mouse button at the current cursor position and leave it held indefinitely. Returns immediately. Pair with `input.mouse.release` (or rely on connection-close cleanup) to lift. Use this for multi-verb chord workflows that need the button held across other operations; for single-verb timed holds use `input.mouse.click {duration_ms}`. Per issue #67.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. The agent records the button as held on this connection; see lifecycle §2.8 for cleanup semantics.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_MOUSE + the appropriate `MOUSEEVENTF_*DOWN` flag (`MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN`, `MOUSEEVENTF_RIGHTDOWN`, `MOUSEEVENTF_MIDDLEDOWN`). No matching up event — the button stays held until `input.mouse.release` or connection close.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where SendInput is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with MOUSEEVENTF_*DOWN. Agent registers the button in the per-connection held-input set so lifecycle §2.8 can release it on connection close. Repeated `press` of an already-held button is a no-op (the OS treats it the same; agent state already reflects held). UIPI applies — synthesised input directed at higher-IL windows is silently dropped, returns `ERR uipi_blocked`.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; mouse_event on NT 4 / 9x. Same per-connection held-input tracking as modern. No UIPI on classic — synthesised input crosses process boundaries freely.
